# @ternent/concord

> Shared, signed, partly private documents built from an application's events and reducer.

Exports: `createDocument`, `openDocument`, `defineModel`. Types include `Model`, `Event`,
`Document`, `Group`, `GroupId`, `Member`, `Role`, `Rejection`, `Returned`, `Json`.
Declarations: `dist/index.d.ts`.

```ts
import { createIdentity } from "@ternent/identity";
import { createDocument, defineModel, openDocument } from "@ternent/concord";

const tasks = defineModel({
  id: "tasks",
  version: 1,
  initial: () => ({ tasks: {} }),
  reduce(state, event) {
    if (event.type === "task.add") return { tasks: { ...state.tasks, [event.data.id]: event.data } };
    throw new Error(`Unknown event ${event.type}`);
  },
});

const alice = await createIdentity();
const doc = await createDocument({ model: tasks, identity: alice });
doc.stage({ type: "task.add", data: { id: "1", title: "Plan" } });
await doc.commit(); // stage + commit is an immediate write

const leads = await doc.createGroup();
doc.stage({ type: "task.add", data: { id: "2", title: "Private" } }, { group: leads });
await doc.commit();
const bytes = doc.export(); // store or sync these bytes; Concord does neither
```

- `reduce` must be synchronous and pure, never mutate `state` (it is frozen), and throw to reject.
- `reduce` only sees its own group's state. Rules that must bind a group can only use that
  group's events. Combine group states for display in the app.
- A draft holds events for one group. `createGroup`, `setMember`, `removeMember` and
  `rebase` throw while a draft has events.
- `state(group)` throws for a group you cannot read; that is different from an empty group.
- Check `doc.rejected`: signed commits that broke a group's rules have no effect.
- Roles: `"member"` and `"admin"`. Only admins change membership; the last admin stays.
- Adding a member reveals the group's whole history to them. Removal rotates the key for the
  future only.
- Bump `version` when `reduce` rules change, and keep handling old events; older apps refuse
  newer groups.
- After two copies diverge, call `rebase(otherBytes, { published: lastPublishedHead })` and
  show the returned commits to the user.
- Without keys, the file still shows signer keys, times, history shape and sizes. Don't
  promise users more privacy than that.
